Avoiding the hyperplane {x1=0}\{x_1 = 0\}{x1​=0}
This section uses mainly vocabulary and concepts from algebraic geometry. We will define the most important quantities used here (for a comprehensive overview of the concepts of algebraic geometry, we refer to textbooks such as [hartshorne]), then state the two main results. Theorem 5.7 shows that for a closed irreducible subvariety Y⊆XY\subseteq XY⊆X not meeting the hyperplane {x1=0}\{x_1=0\}{x1​=0}, the covector dx1dx_1dx1​ is an asymptotic conormal direction of YYY. Theorem 5.8 uses it to show that no nonempty closed, fibre-conical, involutive subset W⊆T∗XW\subseteq T^*XW⊆T∗X whose projection to XXX does not meet the hyperplane {x1=0}\{x_1 = 0\}{x1​=0} can be contained in the zero set of a polynomial P(ξ)P(\xi)P(ξ) with P(1,0,…,0)≠0P(1,0,\dots,0)\neq0P(1,0,…,0)=0. We prove the first theorem in Subsection 5.2, with the lemmas stated and proved where they are used, and the second in Subsection 5.3.
Preliminaries and definitions from algebraic geometry

J⊆K[x,ξ]J\subseteq K[x,\xi]J⊆K[x,ξ]; by Theorem 2.12(a) they are the closed points of the corresponding V(J)V(J)V(J). formalizesgrapha52a18fdd164281c

Items (a)–(f) are Mathlib definitions, shown here; Lean restates only the facts the proofs use: (g)–(h) and the closing sentence. Separability in characteristic zero is used inside the Mathlib results and not restated.

Definition 5.1 ([Lang 2012, VIII.1, V]).

If K⊆LK\subseteq LK⊆L are fields, we call LLL an extension of KKK and write L/KL/KL/K. For z∈Lz\in Lz∈L and B⊆LB\subseteq LB⊆L we say:

  1. zzz is algebraic over KKK if there exists a nonzero polynomial ggg in one variable over KKK with g(z)=0g(z)=0g(z)=0
  2. zzz is transcendental over KKK if no such polynomial exists, i.e. g(z)=0⇒g=0g(z)=0\Rightarrow g=0g(z)=0⇒g=0
  3. The minimal polynomial of an algebraic zzz over KKK is the polynomial of least degree over KKK with g(z)=0g(z)=0g(z)=0 and coefficient 1 for the highest degree term.
  4. κ/K\kappa/Kκ/K is algebraic if every element of κ\kappaκ is algebraic over KKK
  5. κ/K\kappa/Kκ/K is finitely generated if κ=K(z1,…,zm)\kappa=K(z_1,\dots,z_m)κ=K(z1​,…,zm​) for finitely many ziz_izi​, and separable if every z∈κz\in\kappaz∈κ that is algebraic over KKK has a minimal polynomial without repeated roots - in characteristic zero every algebraic extension is separable.
  6. BBB is algebraically independent over KKK if no nonzero polynomial over KKK in finitely many elements of BBB vanishes.
  7. A maximal algebraically independent subset is a transcendence basis of L/KL/KL/K. If BBB is a transcendence basis, then LLL is algebraic over the subfield K(B)K(B)K(B) generated by KKK and BBB.
  8. Any two transcendence bases of L/KL/KL/K have the same cardinality, called the transcendence degree trdeg⁡KL\operatorname{trdeg}_KLtrdegK​L.
The elements of κ\kappaκ that are algebraic over KKK form a subfield, and every finite set generating κ\kappaκ over KKK contains a transcendence basis.

IsAlgebraic defMathlib/RingTheory/Algebraic/Defs.lean:42
/-- An element of an R-algebra is algebraic over R if it is a root of a nonzero polynomial
with coefficients in R. -/
@[stacks 09GC "Algebraic elements"]
def IsAlgebraic (x : A) : Prop :=
  ∃ p : R[X], p ≠ 0 ∧ aeval x p = 0
Transcendental defMathlib/RingTheory/Algebraic/Defs.lean:48
/-- An element of an R-algebra is transcendental over R if it is not algebraic over R. -/
def Transcendental (x : A) : Prop :=
  ¬IsAlgebraic R x
minpoly defMathlib/FieldTheory/Minpoly/Basic.lean:31
/-- Suppose `x : B`, where `B` is an `A`-algebra.

The minimal polynomial `minpoly A x` of `x`
is a monic polynomial with coefficients in `A` of smallest degree that has `x` as its root,
if such exists (`IsIntegral A x`) or zero otherwise.

For example, if `V` is a `𝕜`-vector space for some field `𝕜` and `f : V →ₗ[𝕜] V` then
the minimal polynomial of `f` is `minpoly 𝕜 f`.
-/
@[stacks 09GM]
noncomputable def minpoly (x : B) : A[X] :=
  if hx : IsIntegral A x then degree_lt_wf.min _ hx else 0
Algebra.IsAlgebraic classMathlib/RingTheory/Algebraic/Defs.lean:66
/-- An algebra is algebraic if all its elements are algebraic. -/
@[stacks 09GC "Algebraic extensions"]
protected class Algebra.IsAlgebraic : Prop where
  isAlgebraic : ∀ x : A, IsAlgebraic R x
AlgebraicIndependent defMathlib/RingTheory/AlgebraicIndependent/Defs.lean:51
/-- `AlgebraicIndependent R x` states the family of elements `x`
  is algebraically independent over `R`, meaning that the canonical
  map out of the multivariable polynomial ring is injective. -/
@[stacks 030E "(1)"] def AlgebraicIndependent : Prop :=
  Injective (MvPolynomial.aeval x : MvPolynomial ι R →ₐ[R] A)
IsTranscendenceBasis defMathlib/RingTheory/AlgebraicIndependent/Defs.lean:172
/-- A family is a transcendence basis if it is a maximal algebraically independent subset. -/
@[stacks 030E "(4)"] def IsTranscendenceBasis (x : ι → A) : Prop :=
  AlgebraicIndependent R x ∧
    ∀ (s : Set A) (_ : AlgebraicIndepOn R id s) (_ : range x ⊆ s), range x = s
Algebra.trdeg defMathlib/RingTheory/AlgebraicIndependent/Basic.lean:43
/-- The transcendence degree of a commutative algebra `A` over a commutative ring `R` is
defined to be the maximal cardinality of an `R`-algebraically independent set in `A`. -/
@[stacks 030G] def Algebra.trdeg : Cardinal.{v} :=
  ⨆ ι : { s : Set A // AlgebraicIndepOn R _root_.id s }, Cardinal.mk ι.1

/-- **Definition 5.1(g)–(h).** For a transcendence basis `B` of `L/K`, `L` is algebraic
over `K(B)`, and `|B| = trdeg_K L`. -/
theorem definition_5_1_g_h {B : Set L} (hB : IsTranscendenceBasis K ((↑) : B → L)) :
    Algebra.IsAlgebraic (IntermediateField.adjoin K (Set.range ((↑) : B → L))) L ∧
      Cardinal.mk B = Algebra.trdeg K L :=
  ⟨hB.isAlgebraic_field, hB.cardinalMk_eq_trdeg⟩

Lean source
/-- **Definition 5.1, closing sentence.** The elements of `L` that are algebraic over
`K` form a subfield, and every finite set generating `L` over `K` contains a
transcendence basis ([Lang, Thm. VIII.1.1]). -/
theorem definition_5_1_closing :
    (∃ E : IntermediateField K L, ∀ z : L, z ∈ E ↔ IsAlgebraic K z) ∧
      ∀ S : Set L, S.Finite → IntermediateField.adjoin K S = ⊤ →
        ∃ B ⊆ S, IsTranscendenceBasis K ((↑) : B → L) := by
  refine ⟨⟨algebraicClosure K L, fun z => mem_algebraicClosure_iff⟩, fun S _ hS => ?_⟩
  have : Algebra.IsAlgebraic (Algebra.adjoin K S) L := by
    rw [← IntermediateField.isAlgebraic_adjoin_iff_top, hS]
    exact ⟨fun z => ⟨Polynomial.X - Polynomial.C ⟨z, trivial⟩, Polynomial.X_sub_C_ne_zero _,
      by simp [Polynomial.aeval_def]⟩⟩
  exact exists_isTranscendenceBasis_subset S

Definition 5.2 ([Matsumura 1986, §25]).

Let κ/K\kappa/Kκ/K be a field extension.

  1. A KKK-derivation of κ\kappaκ is a KKK-linear map D ⁣:κ→κD\colon\kappa\to\kappaD:κ→κ with D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a).
  2. Let G\mathcal GG be the free κ\kappaκ-vector space with basis symbols ⟨a⟩\langle a\rangle⟨a⟩, a∈κa\in\kappaa∈κ. The space of differentials Ωκ/K\Omega_{\kappa/K}Ωκ/K​ is the quotient of G\mathcal GG by the subspace spanned by
    ⟨a+b⟩−⟨a⟩−⟨b⟩,⟨ab⟩−a⟨b⟩−b⟨a⟩,⟨c⟩(a,b∈κ, c∈K), \langle a+b\rangle-\langle a\rangle-\langle b\rangle,\quad \langle ab\rangle-a\langle b\rangle-b\langle a\rangle,\quad \langle c\rangle\qquad(a,b\in\kappa,\ c\in K), ⟨a+b⟩−⟨a⟩−⟨b⟩,⟨ab⟩−a⟨b⟩−b⟨a⟩,⟨c⟩(a,b∈κ, c∈K),
    and da∈Ωκ/Kda\in\Omega_{\kappa/K}da∈Ωκ/K​ denotes the class of ⟨a⟩\langle a\rangle⟨a⟩.
  3. A KKK-derivation DDD induces the κ\kappaκ-linear map Ωκ/K→κ\Omega_{\kappa/K}\to\kappaΩκ/K​→κ, da↦D(a)da\mapsto D(a)da↦D(a), since the linear map ⟨a⟩↦D(a)\langle a\rangle\mapsto D(a)⟨a⟩↦D(a) on G\mathcal GG kills the relations. Conversely, a κ\kappaκ-linear map Ωκ/K→κ\Omega_{\kappa/K}\to\kappaΩκ/K​→κ gives the KKK-derivation a↦(its value on da)a\mapsto(\text{its value on }da)a↦(its value on da). Hence a basis dβ1,…,dβdd\beta_1,\dots,d\beta_ddβ1​,…,dβd​ of Ωκ/K\Omega_{\kappa/K}Ωκ/K​ has dual derivations D1,…,DdD_1,\dots,D_dD1​,…,Dd​ with Dk(βl)=δklD_k(\beta_l)=\delta_{kl}Dk​(βl​)=δkl​.

Derivation structureMathlib/RingTheory/Derivation/Basic.lean:40
/-- `D : Derivation R A M` is an `R`-linear map from `A` to `M` that satisfies the `leibniz`
equality. We also require that `D 1 = 0`. See `Derivation.mk'` for a constructor that deduces this
assumption from the Leibniz rule when `M` is cancellative.

TODO: update this when bimodules are defined. -/
structure Derivation (R : Type*) (A : Type*) (M : Type*)
    [CommSemiring R] [CommSemiring A] [AddCommMonoid M] [Algebra R A] [Module A M] [Module R M]
    extends A →ₗ[R] M where
  protected map_one_eq_zero' : toLinearMap 1 = 0
  protected leibniz' (a b : A) : toLinearMap (a * b) = a • toLinearMap b + b • toLinearMap a
Stafford38.Paper.Section5.differentialRelations defStafford38/Paper/Section5/Definitions.lean:246
/-- The relations of Definition 5.2(b) in the free `κ`-vector space `𝒢` on symbols
`⟨a⟩ = Finsupp.single a 1`: `⟨a+b⟩ - ⟨a⟩ - ⟨b⟩`, `⟨ab⟩ - a⟨b⟩ - b⟨a⟩`, `⟨c⟩` (`c ∈ K`). -/
def differentialRelations (K κ : Type*) [Field K] [Field κ] [Algebra K κ] :
    Submodule κ (κ →₀ κ) :=
  Submodule.span κ
    (((Set.range fun x : κ × κ ↦
        Finsupp.single (x.1 + x.2) 1 - Finsupp.single x.1 1 - Finsupp.single x.2 1) ∪
      Set.range fun x : κ × κ ↦
        Finsupp.single (x.1 * x.2) 1 - x.1 • Finsupp.single x.2 1 -
          x.2 • Finsupp.single x.1 1) ∪
      Set.range fun c : K ↦ Finsupp.single (algebraMap K κ c) 1)

Lean source
/-- **Definition 5.2(b).** `Ω_{κ/K}`, the quotient of the free module `𝒢` by the printed
relations, is Mathlib's `Ω[κ⁄K]`, with the class of `⟨a⟩` going to `da`. -/
theorem definition_5_2_b :
    ∃ e : ((L →₀ L) ⧸ differentialRelations K L) ≃ₗ[L] Ω[L⁄K],
      ∀ a : L, e (Submodule.Quotient.mk (Finsupp.single a 1)) = KaehlerDifferential.D K L a := by
  refine ⟨(Submodule.quotEquivOfEq _ _ differentialRelations_eq_kerTotal).trans
    (KaehlerDifferential.quotKerTotalEquiv K L), fun a ↦ ?_⟩
  simp [KaehlerDifferential.quotKerTotalEquiv]
Stafford38.Paper.Section5.definition_5_2_c_correspondence theoremStafford38/Paper/Section5/Definitions.lean:306
Stafford38.Paper.Section5.definition_5_2_c_correspondence.{u_2, u_3} {K : Type u_2} {L : Type u_3}
  [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L] :
  ∃ e,
    (∀ (φ : Ω[L⁄K] →ₗ[L] L) (a : L), (e φ) a = φ ((KaehlerDifferential.D K L) a)) ∧
      ∀ (D : Derivation K L L) (a : L), (e.symm D) ((KaehlerDifferential.D K L) a) = D a
Lean source
/-- **Definition 5.2(c), first sentences.** A `K`-derivation `D` of `κ` induces the
`κ`-linear map `Ω_{κ/K} → κ`, `da ↦ D(a)`, and conversely a `κ`-linear map
`φ : Ω_{κ/K} → κ` gives the `K`-derivation `a ↦ φ(da)`; the two constructions are
inverse (`KaehlerDifferential.linearMapEquivDerivation`). -/
theorem definition_5_2_c_correspondence :
    ∃ e : (Ω[L⁄K] →ₗ[L] L) ≃ₗ[L] Derivation K L L,
      (∀ (φ : Ω[L⁄K] →ₗ[L] L) (a : L), e φ a = φ (KaehlerDifferential.D K L a)) ∧
        ∀ (D : Derivation K L L) (a : L), e.symm D (KaehlerDifferential.D K L a) = D a :=
  ⟨KaehlerDifferential.linearMapEquivDerivation K L, fun _ _ => rfl,
    fun D a => D.liftKaehlerDifferential_comp_D a⟩

Stafford38.Paper.Section5.definition_5_2_c.{u_2, u_3, u_4} {K : Type u_2} {L : Type u_3} [Field K]
  [Field L] [Algebra K L] {ι : Type u_4} [DecidableEq ι] (β : ι → L) (b : Module.Basis ι L Ω[L⁄K])
  (hb : ∀ (l : ι), b l = (KaehlerDifferential.D K L) (β l)) :
  ∃ D, ∀ (k' l : ι), (D k') (β l) = if k' = l then 1 else 0
Lean source
/-- **Definition 5.2(c).** A basis `dβ_1, …, dβ_d` of `Ω_{κ/K}` has dual derivations
`D_k` with `D_k(β_l) = δ_{kl}`, namely `D_k = (dβ_k)^* ∘ d`. -/
theorem definition_5_2_c {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] (β : ι → L)
    (b : Module.Basis ι L Ω[L⁄K]) (hb : ∀ l, b l = KaehlerDifferential.D K L (β l)) :
    ∃ D : ι → Derivation K L L, ∀ k' l, D k' (β l) = if k' = l then 1 else 0 := by
  -- `dβ_l` is the class of `⟨β_l⟩` (Definition 5.2(b)); `D_k` is the derivation
  -- of the coordinate functional `(dβ_k)^*` on `Ω_{κ/K}`.
  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := definition_5_2_b (K := K) (L := L)
  obtain ⟨c, hc, -⟩ := definition_5_2_c_correspondence (K := K) (L := L)
  refine ⟨fun k' ↦ c (b.coord k'), fun k' l ↦ ?_⟩
  have hb' : ∀ l, b l = e (Submodule.Quotient.mk (Finsupp.single (β l) 1)) :=
    fun l ↦ (hb l).trans (he _).symm
  rw [hc, ← he, ← hb', Module.Basis.coord_apply, Module.Basis.repr_self, Finsupp.single_apply]
  by_cases h : k' = l
  · subst h; simp
  · simp [h, Ne.symm h]

Definition 5.3 ([Matsumura 1986, §10-§11]).

Let FFF be a field.

  1. A subring W⊆FW\subseteq FW⊆F is a valuation ring of FFF if for every a∈F×a\in F^\timesa∈F× we have a∈Wa\in Wa∈W or a−1∈Wa^{-1}\in Wa−1∈W. It is a local ring with maximal ideal mW=W∖W×\mathfrak m_W=W\setminus W^\timesmW​=W∖W×.
  2. A discrete valuation ring (DVR) is a Noetherian valuation ring V≠FV\ne FV=F. Then mV\mathfrak m_VmV​ is generated by some ϖ∈V\varpi\in Vϖ∈V, and every f∈F×f\in F^\timesf∈F× is f=ϖkuf=\varpi^kuf=ϖku with k∈Zk\in\mathbb Zk∈Z and u∈V×u\in V^\timesu∈V×, and ord⁡V(f):=k\operatorname{ord}_V(f):=kordV​(f):=k.
  3. For a field κ=V/mV\kappa = V/\mathfrak m_Vκ=V/mV​ we write κ[[t]]\kappa[[t]]κ[[t]] for the ring of formal power series, and κ((t))\kappa((t))κ((t)) for its fraction field (formal Laurent series).

  is not a field. -/
class IsDiscreteValuationRing (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] : Prop
    extends IsPrincipalIdealRing R, IsLocalRing R where
  not_a_field' : maximalIdeal R ≠ ⊥

/-- **Definition 5.3.** Let `F` be a field.
(a) A subring `W ⊆ F` is a valuation ring of `F` iff `a ∈ W` or `a⁻¹ ∈ W` for
every `a ∈ F^×`; it is a local ring with maximal ideal `𝔪_W = W ∖ W^×`.
(b) A valuation ring `V` is a discrete valuation ring iff it is Noetherian and
`V ≠ F`; then `𝔪_V` is generated by some `ϖ ∈ V`, and every `f ∈ F^×` is
`f = ϖ^k u` with `u ∈ V^×` and a unique `k = ord_V(f) ∈ ℤ`.
(c) For a field `κ`, `κ((t))` (`LaurentSeries κ`) is the fraction field of
`κ[[t]]` (`PowerSeries κ`). -/
theorem definition_5_3 {F : Type u} [Field F] :
    (∀ S : Subring F,
        (∀ a : F, a ≠ 0 → a ∈ S ∨ a⁻¹ ∈ S) ↔ ∃ W : ValuationSubring F, W.toSubring = S) ∧
      (∀ W : ValuationSubring F,
        IsLocalRing W.toSubring ∧ ∀ w : W.toSubring, w ∈ maximalIdeal W.toSubring ↔ ¬ IsUnit w) ∧
      (∀ V : ValuationSubring F,
        IsDiscreteValuationRing V.toSubring ↔ IsNoetherianRing V.toSubring ∧ V ≠ ⊤) ∧
      (∀ V : ValuationSubring F, IsDiscreteValuationRing V.toSubring →
        ∃ ϖ : V.toSubring, maximalIdeal V.toSubring = Ideal.span {ϖ} ∧
          ∀ f : F, f ≠ 0 → ∃! k : ℤ, ∃ u : V.toSubringˣ,
            f = (ϖ : F) ^ k * ((u : V.toSubring) : F)) ∧
      ∀ (κ : Type u) [Field κ], IsFractionRing (PowerSeries κ) (LaurentSeries κ) := by
  refine ⟨fun S => ⟨fun h => ?_, ?_⟩, fun W => ⟨inferInstance, fun w => ?_⟩,
    fun V => ⟨fun hV => ?_, fun ⟨hN, hV⟩ => ?_⟩, fun V hV => ?_, fun κ _ => inferInstance⟩
  · refine ⟨⟨S, fun a => ?_⟩, rfl⟩
    by_cases ha : a = 0
    · exact Or.inl (ha ▸ S.zero_mem)
    · exact h a ha
  · rintro ⟨W, rfl⟩ a _
    exact W.mem_or_inv_mem a
  · rw [mem_maximalIdeal, mem_nonunits_iff]
  · refine ⟨inferInstance, fun hVtop => IsDiscreteValuationRing.not_isField V.toSubring ?_⟩
    exact (step_5_3_isField_iff V).2 hVtop
  · have hfield : ¬ IsField V.toSubring := fun h => hV ((step_5_3_isField_iff V).1 h)
    have := step_5_3_valuationRing V
    exact ((IsDiscreteValuationRing.TFAE V.toSubring hfield).out 1 2).2 this
  · obtain ⟨ϖ, hϖ⟩ := IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_irreducible V.toSubring
    refine ⟨ϖ, hϖ.maximalIdeal_eq, fun f hf => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨k, u, hku⟩ := step_5_3_ord_exists V hϖ hf
    exact ⟨k, ⟨u, hku⟩, fun l ⟨u', hl⟩ => step_5_3_ord_unique V hϖ (hl.symm.trans hku)⟩

JacobianSmoothPoint is the printed Y_sm with dim Y the Krull dimension of K[x]/𝔭; definition_5_4_b_iff proves it equals Mathlib's smooth locus (SmoothAffinePoint), which the proofs use. The claim "open and dense" is not restated; the proofs use density through fibreLift_mem_vanishingIdeal_equationConormal.

Definition 5.4.

We say

  1. A closed set YYY is irreducible if it is not a union of two proper closed subsets, equivalently if I(Y)I(Y)I(Y) is prime [hartshorne, Cor I.1.4].
  2. For irreducible closed YYY, the smooth locus YsmY_{\mathrm{sm}}Ysm​ is the set of y∈Yy\in Yy∈Y at which the Jacobian matrix of generators of I(Y)I(Y)I(Y) has rank n−dim⁡Yn-\dim Yn−dimY, i.e. the points where YYY has a well-defined tangent space of the expected dimension dim⁡Y\dim YdimY (i.e. without kinks etc.). It is open and dense in YYY. [hartshorne, Ch. I.5]
  3. For y∈Yy\in Yy∈Y the conormal space is
    Ny∗Y=span⁡K{ dfy:f∈I(Y) }⊆(Kn)∗,dfy=∑i∂if(y) dxi,N^*_yY=\operatorname{span}_K\{\,df_y : f\in I(Y)\,\}\subseteq(K^n)^*,\qquad df_y=\textstyle\sum_i\partial_if(y)\,dx_i,Ny∗​Y=spanK​{dfy​:f∈I(Y)}⊆(Kn)∗,dfy​=∑i​∂i​f(y)dxi​,
  4. N(Y)=⋃y∈YsmNy∗Y⊆(Kn)∗N(Y)=\bigcup_{y\in Y_{\mathrm{sm}}}N^*_yY\subseteq (K^n)^*N(Y)=⋃y∈Ysm​​Ny∗​Y⊆(Kn)∗ denotes the conormal cone.

Stafford38.Paper.Section5.IsZariskiClosed defStafford38/Paper/Section5/Definitions.lean:45
/-- A Zariski-closed subset of `X = K^n`: `Y = V_K(J)` for an ideal `J ⊆ K[x]`. -/
def IsZariskiClosed (Y : Set (Fin n → k)) : Prop :=
  ∃ J : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k), Y = MvPolynomial.zeroLocus k J
Stafford38.Paper.Section5.IsIrreducibleClosed defStafford38/Paper/Section5/Definitions.lean:49
/-- **Definition 5.4(a).** A closed set `Y` is irreducible if it is not a union of two
proper closed subsets. -/
def IsIrreducibleClosed (Y : Set (Fin n → k)) : Prop :=
  IsZariskiClosed Y ∧ ¬ ∃ Y₁ Y₂ : Set (Fin n → k), IsZariskiClosed Y₁ ∧ IsZariskiClosed Y₂ ∧
    Y₁ ⊂ Y ∧ Y₂ ⊂ Y ∧ Y = Y₁ ∪ Y₂

  IsIrreducibleClosed Y ↔ (MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal k Y).IsPrime

Lean source
/-- **Definition 5.4(a), "equivalently if `I(Y)` is prime"** ([Hartshorne, Cor. I.1.4]).
As there, `Y` is nonempty (the empty set has `I(∅) = K[x]`, which is not prime). -/
theorem definition_5_4_a {Y : Set (Fin n → k)} (hne : Y.Nonempty) (hY : IsZariskiClosed Y) :
    IsIrreducibleClosed Y ↔ (MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal k Y).IsPrime := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨-, hirr⟩
    refine ⟨fun htop => ?_, fun {f g} hfg => ?_⟩
    · obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hne
      have h1 : (1 : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) ∈ MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal k Y :=
        htop ▸ Submodule.mem_top
      have := MvPolynomial.mem_vanishingIdeal_iff.mp h1 y hy
      simp at this
    · by_contra h
      push Not at h
      obtain ⟨hf, hg⟩ := h
      obtain ⟨J, rfl⟩ := hY
      apply hirr
      have hproper : ∀ e : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k, e ∉ MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal k
          (MvPolynomial.zeroLocus k J) →
          MvPolynomial.zeroLocus k (J ⊔ Ideal.span {e}) ⊂ MvPolynomial.zeroLocus k J := by
        intro e he
        refine ⟨MvPolynomial.zeroLocus_anti_mono le_sup_left, fun hsub => he ?_⟩
        rw [MvPolynomial.mem_vanishingIdeal_iff]
        intro y hy
        exact ((mem_zeroLocus_sup_span_singleton J e y).mp (hsub hy)).2
      refine ⟨_, _, ⟨_, rfl⟩, ⟨_, rfl⟩, hproper f hf, hproper g hg, ?_⟩
      ext y
      simp only [Set.mem_union, mem_zeroLocus_sup_span_singleton]
      constructor
      · intro hy
        have h0 := MvPolynomial.mem_vanishingIdeal_iff.mp hfg y hy
        rw [map_mul] at h0
        rcases mul_eq_zero.mp h0 with h0 | h0
        · exact Or.inl ⟨hy, h0⟩
        · exact Or.inr ⟨hy, h0⟩
      · rintro (⟨hy, -⟩ | ⟨hy, -⟩) <;> exact hy
  · intro hP
    refine ⟨hY, ?_⟩
    rintro ⟨Y₁, Y₂, hY₁, hY₂, h₁, h₂, hU⟩
    -- a proper closed `Y_i` is cut out inside `Y` by some `f_i ∈ I(Y_i) ∖ I(Y)`
    have hsep : ∀ Z : Set (Fin n → k), IsZariskiClosed Z → Z ⊂ Y →
        ∃ f ∈ MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal k Z, f ∉ MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal k Y := by
      intro Z hZ hZY
      obtain ⟨y, hyY, hyZ⟩ := Set.exists_of_ssubset hZY
      rw [← zeroLocus_vanishingIdeal_of_isZariskiClosed hZ, MvPolynomial.mem_zeroLocus_iff] at hyZ
      push Not at hyZ
      obtain ⟨f, hf, hfy⟩ := hyZ
      exact ⟨f, hf, fun hfY => hfy (MvPolynomial.mem_vanishingIdeal_iff.mp hfY y hyY)⟩
    obtain ⟨f₁, hf₁, hf₁Y⟩ := hsep Y₁ hY₁ h₁
    obtain ⟨f₂, hf₂, hf₂Y⟩ := hsep Y₂ hY₂ h₂
    have hprod : f₁ * f₂ ∈ MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal k Y := by
      rw [MvPolynomial.mem_vanishingIdeal_iff]
      intro y hy
      rw [hU] at hy
      rw [map_mul]
      rcases hy with hy | hy
      · rw [MvPolynomial.mem_vanishingIdeal_iff.mp hf₁ y hy, zero_mul]
      · rw [MvPolynomial.mem_vanishingIdeal_iff.mp hf₂ y hy, mul_zero]
    rcases hP.mem_or_mem hprod with h | h
    · exact hf₁Y h
    · exact hf₂Y h
Stafford38.Paper.Section5.JacobianSmoothPoint defStafford38/Paper/Section5/SmoothLocus.lean:359
/-- **Definition 5.4(b), the Jacobian smooth locus.** `y ∈ Y_sm` iff `y ∈ Y = V(𝔭)` and
the Jacobian matrix `(∂_i g_j(y))` of generators `g_1, …, g_s` of `I(Y) = 𝔭` has rank
`n - dim Y`, written `rank + dim Y = n` with `dim Y` the Krull dimension of `K[x]/𝔭`.
The rank does not depend on the generators
(`jacobian_rank_eq_finrank_differentialSpan`, `jacobianSmoothPoint_iff_span`). -/
def JacobianSmoothPoint (P : PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) (y : Fin n → k) : Prop :=
  y ∈ MvPolynomial.zeroLocus k P.asIdeal ∧
    ∃ (s : ℕ) (g : Fin s → MvPolynomial (Fin n) k), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = P.asIdeal ∧
      ((Matrix.of fun j i ↦ differentialAt y (g j) i).rank : WithBot ℕ∞) +
        ringKrullDim (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ P.asIdeal) = n

        { asIdeal := RingHom.ker e.toRingHom, isPrime := hprime } ∈

/-- **Definition 5.4(b), the Jacobian criterion.** `y` lies in Mathlib's smooth locus of
`K[x]/𝔭` iff the Jacobian of `𝔭` has rank `n - dim Y` at `y ∈ Y`.  The converse direction
picks equations `f_1, …, f_c ∈ 𝔭` with independent differentials at `y` and applies
`smoothAffinePoint_of_jacobian`. -/
theorem definition_5_4_b_iff [CharZero k]
    (P : PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) (y : Fin n → k) :
    SmoothAffinePoint P.asIdeal y ↔ JacobianSmoothPoint P y := by
  classical
  refine ⟨definition_5_4_b P, fun h ↦ ?_⟩
  have hle := componentDimension_le P
  rw [jacobianSmoothPoint_iff_trdeg] at h
  obtain ⟨hy, hr⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨s, hsub, hspan, hli⟩ :=
    exists_linearIndependent k (Set.range fun f : P.asIdeal ↦ differentialAt y f.1)
  have : Fintype s := (hli.setFinite).fintype
  have hcard : Fintype.card s = Module.finrank k
      (Submodule.span k (Set.range fun f : P.asIdeal ↦ differentialAt y f.1)) := by
    rw [← hspan, ← finrank_span_eq_card hli, Subtype.range_coe]
  have hg : ∀ v : s, ∃ g : MvPolynomial (Fin n) k, g ∈ P.asIdeal ∧ differentialAt y g = v :=
    fun v ↦ by
      obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hsub v.2
      exact ⟨g.1, g.2, hg⟩
  choose g hgP hgd using hg
  have hli' : LinearIndependent k fun v : s ↦ differentialAt y (g v) := by
    convert hli using 1
    funext v
    exact hgd v
  exact smoothAffinePoint_of_jacobian P hy g hgP hli' (by
    change Fintype.card s + componentDimension P = n
    omega)

/-- **Definition 5.4(c).** `N*_y Y = span_K {df_y : f ∈ I}`, with covectors in
coordinates. -/
theorem definition_5_4_c
    (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) (y ξ : Fin n → k) :
    coordinateCovector ξ ∈ affineConormalSpace y I ↔
      ξ ∈ Submodule.span k (Set.range fun f : I => differentialAt y f.1) := by
  have hspan : equationCovectorSpan y I =
      (Submodule.span k (Set.range fun f : I => differentialAt y f.1)).map
        (coordinateCovectorLinear (k := k) (n := n)) := by
    rw [Submodule.map_span, ← Set.range_comp]
    rfl
  rw [affineConormalSpace_eq_equationCovectorSpan, hspan]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨η, hη, hηξ⟩
    have : η = ξ := coordinateCovector_injective hηξ
    exact this ▸ hη
  · intro hξ
    exact ⟨ξ, hξ, rfl⟩
Stafford38.Paper.Section5.conormalCone defStafford38/Paper/Section5/SmoothLocus.lean:550
/-- **Definition 5.4(d), as printed.** The conormal cone
`N(Y) = ⋃_{y ∈ Y_sm} N*_y Y` over the Jacobian smooth locus, with
`N*_y Y = span_K {df_y : f ∈ I(Y)}`. -/
def conormalCone (P : PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) : Set (Fin n → k) :=
  {ξ | ∃ y, JacobianSmoothPoint P y ∧
    ξ ∈ Submodule.span k (Set.range fun f : P.asIdeal ↦ differentialAt y f.1)}

/-- **Definition 5.4(d).** `N(Y) = ⋃_{y ∈ Y_sm} N*_y Y`, in the paper's form of
`N*_y Y`. -/
theorem definition_5_4_d
    [IsAlgClosed k] (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) (ξ : Fin n → k) :
    ξ ∈ smoothConormalFibreProjection I ↔
      ∃ y, SmoothAffinePoint I y ∧
        ξ ∈ Submodule.span k (Set.range fun f : I => differentialAt y f.1) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨y, hy, hξ⟩
    exact ⟨y, hy, (definition_5_4_c I y ξ).1 hξ⟩
  · rintro ⟨y, hy, hξ⟩
    exact ⟨y, hy, (definition_5_4_c I y ξ).2 hξ⟩

def SmoothAffinePoint (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k))
    (y : Fin n → k) : Prop :=
  ∃ e : (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ I) →ₐ[k] k,

    (⟨RingHom.ker e.toRingHom, hprime⟩ :
      PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ I)) ∈

/-- **Definition 5.5.** The printed `Dir(Y)` is the Lean direction closure used in
Theorem 5.7(ii). -/
theorem definition_5_5 [CharZero k] (P : PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) :
    conormalDirections P = projectiveHomogeneousClosure
      (projectivizedDirectionSet (smoothConormalDirectionSet P.asIdeal)) := by
  rw [projectivizedDirectionSet_smoothConormalDirectionSet, conormalDirections,
    conormalCone_paper_eq]

/-- **Definition 5.6.** `W` is fibre-conical iff it is stable under the
fibrewise scaling `(y, ξ) ↦ (y, tξ)`, `t ∈ K^×`: the scaling maps
`W ∩ T*_y X` into `W ∩ T*_y X` for every fibre `T*_y X = π⁻¹(y)`
(`Section2.fibre`, Definition 2.5). -/
theorem definition_5_6
    [IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k] (W : Set (PhaseVar n → k)) :
    Stafford38.Geometry.FibreConicalVanishingIdeal.IsFibreConical W ↔
      ∀ y ξ : Fin n → k, Sum.elim y ξ ∈ W ∩ Stafford38.Paper.Section2.fibre y →
        ∀ t : k, t ≠ 0 → Sum.elim y (t • ξ) ∈ W ∩ Stafford38.Paper.Section2.fibre y := by
  constructor
  · intro hW y ξ hq t ht
    exact ⟨by simpa [Pi.smul_def] using hW _ hq.1 t ht, rfl⟩
  · intro hW q hq t ht
    have hsplit : q = Sum.elim (fun i => q (.inl i)) (fun i => q (.inr i)) := by
      funext i; cases i <;> rfl
    rw [hsplit] at hq
    simpa [Pi.smul_def] using (hW _ _ ⟨hq, rfl⟩ t ht).1

/-- **Theorem 5.7(i).** Let `Y ⊆ X = K^n` be nonempty, closed and irreducible
(Definition 5.4(a)) with `Y ∩ H = ∅`, `H = {x_1 = 0}`, and let
`N(Y) = ⋃_{y ∈ Y_sm} N*_y Y` be the conormal cone over the smooth locus.  Every
polynomial `P ∈ K[ξ_1, …, ξ_n]` vanishing on `N(Y)` satisfies `P(1, 0, …, 0) = 0`.
Derived from `theorem_5_7_i_prime` with `𝔭 = I(Y)`. -/
theorem theorem_5_7_i_printed
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k]
    {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m)
    (Y : Set (Fin m → k)) (hne : Y.Nonempty) (hY : IsIrreducibleClosed Y)
    (hH : Y ∩ {y | y ⟨0, hm⟩ = 0} = ∅)
    (P : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)
    (hP : ∀ ξ ∈ conormalCone (idealPoint Y hne hY), MvPolynomial.eval ξ P = 0) :
    MvPolynomial.eval (fun i : Fin m => if i = ⟨0, hm⟩ then (1 : k) else 0) P = 0 := by
  refine theorem_5_7_i_prime hm (idealPoint Y hne hY) (fun y hy h0 => ?_) P hP
  change y ∈ MvPolynomial.zeroLocus k (MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal k Y) at hy
  rw [zeroLocus_vanishingIdeal_of_isZariskiClosed hY.1] at hy
  exact (Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mp hH) y ⟨hy, h0⟩

theorem theorem_5_7_ii_printed
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] [CharZero k]
    {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m)
    (Y : Set (Fin m → k)) (hne : Y.Nonempty) (hY : IsIrreducibleClosed Y)
    (hH : Y ∩ {y | y ⟨0, hm⟩ = 0} = ∅) :
    Projectivization.mk k
        (fun i : Fin m => if i = ⟨0, hm⟩ then (1 : k) else 0)
        (by intro h; have := congrFun h ⟨0, hm⟩; simp at this) ∈
      conormalDirections (idealPoint Y hne hY) := by
  refine theorem_5_7_ii_prime hm (idealPoint Y hne hY) (fun y hy h0 => ?_)
  change y ∈ MvPolynomial.zeroLocus k (MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal k Y) at hy
  rw [zeroLocus_vanishingIdeal_of_isZariskiClosed hY.1] at hy
  exact (Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mp hH) y ⟨hy, h0⟩

/-- **Theorem 5.8.** Let `K` be algebraically closed of characteristic zero and
`W ⊆ T*X` Zariski closed, fibre-conical and involutive.  If
`P ∈ K[ξ_1, …, ξ_n]` with `P(1, 0, …, 0) ≠ 0` vanishes on `W` and
`W ∩ π⁻¹(H) = ∅`, then `W = ∅`.  Proved along Subsection 5.3. -/
theorem theorem_5_8
    (hm : 0 < m) (W : Set (PhaseVar m → k))
    (hclosed : ∃ L : Ideal (SymbolRing k m), W = MvPolynomial.zeroLocus k L)
    (hcone : IsFibreConical W)
    (hinv : IsInvolutive (MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal k W))
    (P : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)
    (haxis : MvPolynomial.eval
      (fun i : Fin m => if i = ⟨0, hm⟩ then (1 : k) else 0) P ≠ 0)
    (hPW : ∀ q ∈ W, MvPolynomial.eval (fun i => q (.inr i)) P = 0)
    (hH : W ∩ {q | q (.inl ⟨0, hm⟩) = 0} = ∅) :
    W = ∅ := by
  -- Suppose `W ≠ ∅`.
  by_contra hne
  have hW : W.Nonempty := Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.2 hne
  -- `B` is radical with a minimal prime `𝔮`; `Y_0 = V_K(𝔮)`.
  obtain ⟨hrad, -, -, 𝔮, h𝔮⟩ := step_minimal_primes W hclosed hcone hW
  obtain ⟨hprime, -, -, -, havoid⟩ := step_component hm W hclosed hcone hH 𝔮 h𝔮
  -- The separator `s`, then `P` vanishes on `N(Y_0)`.
  obtain ⟨s, hs𝔮, hs⟩ := step_separator W 𝔮 hrad h𝔮
  have hPN := step_P_vanishes_on_conormal_cone W hclosed hcone hinv 𝔮 h𝔮 s hs𝔮 hs P hPW
  -- Theorem 5.7(i) contradicts `P(1, 0, …, 0) ≠ 0`.
  exact haxis (step_theorem_5_7_applies hm 𝔮 hprime havoid P
    (step_P_vanishes_on_N 𝔮 hprime P hPN))

/-- The Gabber-shaped bracket condition: both bracket entries lie in the
ideal.  This is weaker than the project predicate `IsPoisson`. -/
def IsInvolutive (J : Ideal (SymbolRing k n)) : Prop :=
  ∀ f ∈ J, ∀ g ∈ J, poissonBracket f g ∈ J

abbrev SymbolRing (k : Type*) [CommRing k] (n : ℕ) :=

Lean only The Poisson bracket {f, g} = Σ_i (∂f/∂ξ_i ∂g/∂x_i − ∂f/∂x_i ∂g/∂ξ_i) on K[x, ξ] (Definition 2.9).

Stafford38.Characteristic.poissonBracket Lean onlyStafford38/Characteristic/Polynomial.lean:30
/-- The standard Poisson bracket on affine cotangent space. -/
noncomputable def poissonBracket
    {k : Type*} [CommRing k] {n : ℕ}
    (f g : SymbolRing k n) : SymbolRing k n :=
  ∑ i : Fin n,
    (MvPolynomial.pderiv (Sum.inl i : PhaseVar n) f *
        MvPolynomial.pderiv (Sum.inr i : PhaseVar n) g -
      MvPolynomial.pderiv (Sum.inr i : PhaseVar n) f *
        MvPolynomial.pderiv (Sum.inl i : PhaseVar n) g)

/-- **Lemma 5.9.** If `x̄_1` is transcendental over `K`, there are a valuation
ring `K ⊆ W ⊊ F` with `x̄_1 ∈ 𝔪_W` and an index `j` with `x̄_i / x̄_j ∈ W` for
all `0 ≤ i ≤ n`. -/
theorem lemma_5_9 {k F : Type*} [Field k] [Field F] [Algebra k F] {n : ℕ}
    (x : Fin n → F) (i : Fin n) (htrans : Transcendental k (x i)) :
    ∃ (W : ValuationSubring F) (j : Fin (n + 1)),
      (∀ c : k, algebraMap k F c ∈ W) ∧ W ≠ ⊤ ∧
      (∃ hx : x i ∈ W, (⟨x i, hx⟩ : W.toSubring) ∈ maximalIdeal W.toSubring) ∧
      homogeneousCoordinates x j ≠ 0 ∧
      ∀ a, homogeneousCoordinates x a / homogeneousCoordinates x j ∈ W := by
  classical
  -- `W` dominates `K[x̄_1]` localized at `x̄_1` (Stacks, Tag 00IA).
  obtain ⟨W, hkW, hxW, hxinvW⟩ := stage1_exists_valuationSubring_of_transcendental (x i) htrans
  have hx0 : x i ≠ 0 := fun h ↦ htrans (h ▸ isAlgebraic_zero)
  -- Definition 5.3(a): `𝔪_W = W ∖ W^×`
  have hxmax : (⟨x i, hxW⟩ : W.toSubring) ∈ maximalIdeal W.toSubring := by
    rw [(definition_5_3.2.1 W).2]
    rintro ⟨u, hu⟩
    apply hxinvW
    have hmul : x i * ((u⁻¹ : W.toSubringˣ) : W.toSubring) = 1 := by
      have := congrArg Subtype.val (Units.mul_inv u)
      simpa [hu] using this
    have : (x i)⁻¹ = ((u⁻¹ : W.toSubringˣ) : W.toSubring) :=
      (eq_inv_of_mul_eq_one_right hmul).symm
    rw [this]
    exact ((u⁻¹ : W.toSubringˣ) : W.toSubring).2
  have hWtop : W ≠ ⊤ := by
    rintro rfl
    exact hxinvW (ValuationSubring.mem_top _)
  -- Among the nonzero `x̄_i` choose one that is maximal for `a ≼ b ↔ x̄_a / x̄_b ∈ W`.
  let Y := homogeneousCoordinates x
  let S : Set (Fin (n + 1)) := {a | Y a ≠ 0}
  have hS : S.Nonempty := ⟨0, by simp [S, Y]⟩
  letI : LE (Fin (n + 1)) := ⟨fun a b ↦ Y b ≠ 0 ∧ Y a / Y b ∈ W⟩
  have htr : IsTrans (Fin (n + 1)) LE.le := by
    constructor
    intro a b c hab hbc
    rcases hab with ⟨hb, hab⟩
    rcases hbc with ⟨hc, hbc⟩
    refine ⟨hc, ?_⟩
    have := W.toSubring.mul_mem hab hbc
    rwa [div_mul_div_cancel₀ hb] at this
  letI : IsTrans (Fin (n + 1)) LE.le := htr
  obtain ⟨j, hjS, hjmax⟩ := S.toFinite.exists_maximalFor id S hS
  refine ⟨W, j, hkW, hWtop, ⟨hxW, hxmax⟩, hjS, fun a ↦ ?_⟩
  by_cases ha : Y a = 0
  · change Y a / Y j ∈ W
    rw [ha, zero_div]
    exact W.zero_mem
  -- Definition 5.3(a): `a/b ∈ W` or `b/a ∈ W` for nonzero `a, b`
  rcases (definition_5_3.1 W.toSubring).2 ⟨W, rfl⟩ (Y a / Y j) (div_ne_zero ha hjS) with h | h
  · exact h
  · rw [inv_div] at h
    exact (hjmax (show a ∈ S from ha) ⟨ha, h⟩).2

/-- Homogeneous coordinates `(x̄_0, …, x̄_n) = (1, x̄_1, …, x̄_n)`. -/
abbrev homogeneousCoordinates {F : Type*} [Field F] {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → F) :
    Fin (n + 1) → F :=
  Fin.cases 1 x

/-- **Lemma 5.10.**  For `q_i = x̄_i / x̄_j` from Lemma 5.9 there is a discrete
valuation ring `K ⊆ V ⊊ F` (`Frac V = F` holds for every valuation subring) with
(a) `q_i ∈ V` and `x̄_1 ∈ 𝔪_V`, (b) `κ` algebraic over `K(res q_0, …, res q_n)`,
(c) `Ω_{V/K}` finitely generated; the conclusions are the fields of
`Lemma510Place`, which also records `V = A_{𝔭_D}` from the proof.  The clause
`R ⊄ V` of (a) is `lemma_5_10_a_not_R_le`, stated for every valuation ring with
`x̄_1 ∈ 𝔪_V`, which is how the proof of Theorem 5.7 uses it. -/
theorem lemma_5_10 {k F : Type u} [Field k] [CharZero k] [Field F] [Algebra k F]
    {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → F) (i : Fin n)
    (hgen : IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range x) = ⊤)
    (htrans : Transcendental k (x i))
    (W : ValuationSubring F) (j : Fin (n + 1))
    (hkW : ∀ c : k, algebraMap k F c ∈ W)
    (hxW : ∃ hx : x i ∈ W, (⟨x i, hx⟩ : W.toSubring) ∈ maximalIdeal W.toSubring)
    (hj : homogeneousCoordinates x j ≠ 0)
    (hqW : ∀ a, homogeneousCoordinates x a / homogeneousCoordinates x j ∈ W) :
    Nonempty (Lemma510Place k x i j) := by
  classical
  let Y := homogeneousCoordinates x
  obtain ⟨hxiW, hxmW⟩ := hxW
  have hy0 : x i ≠ 0 := fun h ↦ htrans (h ▸ isAlgebraic_zero)
  have hxiInvW : (x i)⁻¹ ∉ W := by
    intro h
    rw [(definition_5_3.2.1 W).2] at hxmW
    apply hxmW
    refine IsUnit.of_mul_eq_one (⟨(x i)⁻¹, h⟩ : W.toSubring) ?_
    apply Subtype.ext
    simp [hy0]
  let s : F := (Y j)⁻¹
  have hs : s ≠ 0 := inv_ne_zero hj
  have hjs : Y j * s = 1 := mul_inv_cancel₀ hj
  have hYsW : ∀ a, Y a * s ∈ W := fun a ↦ by simpa [s, div_eq_mul_inv] using hqW a
  -- `C_0 = K[q_0, …, q_n, x̄_1] ⊆ W`, and `A` is its integral closure in `F`.
  let C₀ : Subalgebra k F :=
    Algebra.adjoin k (Set.range (fun a : Fin (n + 1) ↦ Y a * s) ∪ {x i})
  let SW : Subalgebra k F := { W.toSubring with algebraMap_mem' := hkW }
  have hC₀W : C₀ ≤ SW := by
    apply Algebra.adjoin_le
    rintro z (⟨a, rfl⟩ | hz)
    · exact hYsW a
    · rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hz]
      exact hxiW
  have htop : IntermediateField.adjoin k
      (Set.range (fun a : Fin (n + 1) ↦ Y a * s) ∪ {x i}) = ⊤ := by
    apply top_unique
    rw [← hgen]
    apply IntermediateField.adjoin_le_iff.2
    rintro _ ⟨a, rfl⟩
    apply IntermediateField.mem_adjoin_iff_div.mpr
    refine ⟨Y (Fin.succ a) * s, ?_, s, ?_, ?_⟩
    · exact Algebra.subset_adjoin (R := k) (A := F)
        (Set.mem_union_left _ (Set.mem_range_self _))
    · have h0 : Y 0 * s ∈ C₀ := Algebra.subset_adjoin (R := k) (A := F)
        (Set.mem_union_left _ (Set.mem_range_self (0 : Fin (n + 1))))
      simpa only [Y, homogeneousCoordinates, Fin.cases_zero, one_mul] using h0
    · simp only [Y, Fin.cases_succ]
      exact (eq_div_iff hs).2 rfl
  letI : IsFractionRing C₀ F := IsFractionRing.of_field C₀ F fun z ↦ by
    have hz : z ∈ IntermediateField.adjoin k
        (Set.range (fun a : Fin (n + 1) ↦ Y a * s) ∪ {x i}) := by
      rw [htop]
      exact Set.mem_univ z
    rw [IntermediateField.mem_adjoin_iff_div] at hz
    rcases hz with ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hab⟩
    exact ⟨⟨a, ha⟩, ⟨b, hb⟩, hab⟩
  let A₀ : Subalgebra C₀ F := integralClosure C₀ F
  let A : Subalgebra k F := A₀.restrictScalars k
  have hC₀A : C₀ ≤ A := fun z hz ↦ A₀.algebraMap_mem ⟨z, hz⟩
  -- `W` is integrally closed, so `A ⊆ W` (Atiyah–Macdonald, Prop. 5.18).
  letI : IsIntegrallyClosedIn W.toSubring F := inferInstanceAs (IsIntegrallyClosedIn W F)
  have hA₀W : A₀.toSubring ≤ W.toSubring := by
    change (integralClosure C₀ F).toSubring ≤ W.toSubring
    apply (Subring.integralClosure_subring_le_iff (S := C₀) (T := W.toSubring)).2
    exact hC₀W
  have hyA : x i ∈ A := A₀.algebraMap_mem
    ⟨x i, Algebra.subset_adjoin (Set.mem_union_right _ (Set.mem_singleton _))⟩
  have hnormA : ∀ a, Y a * s ∈ A := fun a ↦ A₀.algebraMap_mem
    ⟨Y a * s, Algebra.subset_adjoin (Set.mem_union_left _ (Set.mem_range_self a))⟩
  have hinvA : (x i)⁻¹ ∉ A := fun h ↦ hxiInvW (hA₀W h)
  -- `A` is a finite `C_0`-module (Hartshorne, Thm. I.3.9A).
  haveI hC₀ft : Algebra.FiniteType k C₀ := Algebra.FiniteType.adjoin_of_finite
    (Set.Finite.union (Set.finite_range _) (Set.finite_singleton _))
  let D : Subalgebra C₀ (FractionRing C₀) := integralClosure C₀ (FractionRing C₀)
  haveI : Module.Finite C₀ D := finite_normalization_of_fg_domain k C₀ D
  let e : FractionRing C₀ ≃ₐ[C₀] F := IsLocalization.algEquiv C₀⁰ (FractionRing C₀) F
  haveI : Module.Finite C₀ A₀ := Module.Finite.equiv e.mapIntegralClosure.toLinearEquiv
  have hsub : A.toSubring = A₀.toSubring := rfl
  let er : A ≃+* A₀ := RingEquiv.subringCongr hsub
  letI : Algebra C₀ A := (er.symm.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap C₀ A₀)).toAlgebra
  let ea : A₀ ≃ₐ[C₀] A := AlgEquiv.ofRingEquiv (f := er.symm) (fun _ ↦ rfl)
  letI : IsScalarTower k C₀ A := IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ ↦ by
    apply Subtype.ext
    rfl
  letI : IsScalarTower C₀ A F := IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ ↦ rfl
  haveI : Module.Finite C₀ A := Module.Finite.equiv ea.toLinearEquiv
  haveI hAft : Algebra.FiniteType k A :=
    Algebra.FiniteType.trans hC₀ft (inferInstance : Algebra.FiniteType C₀ A)
  have hAic : IsIntegrallyClosedIn A F := by
    apply Subring.isIntegrallyClosedIn_iff.mpr
    intro z hz
    change z ∈ integralClosure C₀ F
    exact isIntegral_trans (R := C₀) (A := A) z hz
  letI : IsFractionRing A F := IsFractionRing.of_field A F fun z ↦ by
    obtain ⟨a, b, hb, hab⟩ := IsFractionRing.div_surjective C₀ z
    refine ⟨⟨a, hC₀A a.2⟩, ⟨b, hC₀A b.2⟩, ?_⟩
    change z = (a : F) / (b : F)
    exact hab.symm
  have haint : ∀ a : A, IsIntegral C₀ (a : F) := fun a ↦ a.2
  letI : IsNoetherianRing A := Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing k A
  letI : IsIntegrallyClosed A := (isIntegrallyClosed_iff_isIntegrallyClosedIn F).mpr hAic
  -- `x̄_1` is a nonzero nonunit of `A`; a minimal prime over it has height one (Krull).
  let xA : A := ⟨x i, hyA⟩

Stafford38.Paper.Section5.Lemma510Place structureStafford38/Paper/Section5/Place.lean:102
/-- The discrete valuation ring of Lemma 5.10 together with the construction
`V = A_{𝔭_D}` of its proof: `A` is the integral closure in `F` of
`C_0 = K[q_0, …, q_n, x̄_1]` and `𝔭_D` is a height-one prime of `A` containing
`x̄_1`.  The fields `isDVR`, `q_mem`, `x_mem_p`, `residue_algebraic` and
`kaehler_finite` are the conclusions (a)–(c) of the lemma; the clause `R ⊄ V`
of (a) is `lemma_5_10_a_not_R_le`. -/
structure Lemma510Place (k : Type u) {F : Type u} [Field k] [Field F] [Algebra k F] {n : ℕ}
    (x : Fin n → F) (i : Fin n) (j : Fin (n + 1)) where
  A : Subalgebra k F
  [finiteType : Algebra.FiniteType k A]
  [fractionRing : IsFractionRing A F]
  p : Ideal A
  [isPrime : p.IsPrime]
  place : ∀ z : F, z ∈ (placeSubalgebra A p).toSubring ∨
    z⁻¹ ∈ (placeSubalgebra A p).toSubring
  isDVR : IsDiscreteValuationRing (placeValuationSubring A p place).toSubring
  q_mem : ∀ a, homogeneousCoordinates x a / homogeneousCoordinates x j ∈ A
  x_mem : x i ∈ A
  x_mem_p : (⟨x i, x_mem⟩ : A) ∈ p
  residue_algebraic :
    letI : Algebra k (placeValuationSubring A p place).toSubring :=
      ((algebraMap k F).codRestrict (placeValuationSubring A p place).toSubring
        (fun c ↦ ofField_mem_algebraMap_v A p place (algebraMap k A c))).toAlgebra
    Algebra.IsAlgebraic
      (IntermediateField.adjoin k
        (Set.range fun a ↦ residue (placeValuationSubring A p place).toSubring
          ⟨homogeneousCoordinates x a / homogeneousCoordinates x j,
            ofField_mem_algebraMap_v A p place ⟨_, q_mem a⟩⟩) :
        IntermediateField k (ResidueField (placeValuationSubring A p place).toSubring))
      (ResidueField (placeValuationSubring A p place).toSubring)
  kaehler_finite :
    letI : Algebra k (placeValuationSubring A p place).toSubring :=
      ((algebraMap k F).codRestrict (placeValuationSubring A p place).toSubring
        (fun c ↦ ofField_mem_algebraMap_v A p place (algebraMap k A c))).toAlgebra
    Module.Finite (placeValuationSubring A p place).toSubring
      (Ω[(placeValuationSubring A p place).toSubring⁄k])
Stafford38.Paper.Section5.Lemma510Place.V defStafford38/Paper/Section5/Place.lean:141
/-- The discrete valuation ring `V` of Lemma 5.10. -/
abbrev Lemma510Place.V {k F : Type u} [Field k] [Field F] [Algebra k F] {n : ℕ}
    {x : Fin n → F} {i : Fin n} {j : Fin (n + 1)} (L : Lemma510Place k x i j) :
    ValuationSubring F :=
  placeValuationSubring L.A L.p L.place

  [Field F] [Algebra k F] {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → F) (i : Fin n) (V : ValuationSubring F)
  (hxV : x i ∈ V.toSubring) (hxm : ⟨x i, hxV⟩ ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ↥V.toSubring)

/-- **Lemma 5.10(a), `R ⊄ V`.**  For any valuation ring `V` of `F` with
`x̄_1 ∈ 𝔪_V`: `x̄_1 ∈ R^×` since `1 = ḡ x̄_1` with `ḡ ∈ R`, while `x̄_1 ∈ 𝔪_V`, so
`R ⊄ V`.  The paper derives `1 = ḡ x̄_1` from `Y ∩ H = ∅` by the
Nullstellensatz. -/
theorem lemma_5_10_a_not_R_le {k F : Type*} [Field k] [Field F] [Algebra k F] {n : ℕ}
    (x : Fin n → F) (i : Fin n) (V : ValuationSubring F) (hxV : x i ∈ V.toSubring)
    (hxm : (⟨x i, hxV⟩ : V.toSubring) ∈ maximalIdeal V.toSubring)
    (hunit : ∃ g ∈ Algebra.adjoin k (Set.range x), x i * g = 1) :
    ¬ (Algebra.adjoin k (Set.range x)).toSubring ≤ V.toSubring := by
  obtain ⟨g, hgR, hxg⟩ := hunit
  have hy0 : x i ≠ 0 := left_ne_zero_of_mul_eq_one hxg
  have hinvR : (x i)⁻¹ ∈ Algebra.adjoin k (Set.range x) := by
    rw [← eq_inv_of_mul_eq_one_right hxg]
    exact hgR
  intro hRV
  rw [mem_maximalIdeal, mem_nonunits_iff] at hxm
  apply hxm
  refine IsUnit.of_mul_eq_one (⟨(x i)⁻¹, hRV hinvR⟩ : V.toSubring) ?_
  apply Subtype.ext
  simp [hy0]

    (h : ∀ z : K, z ∈ (placeSubalgebra A p).toSubring ∨
      z⁻¹ ∈ (placeSubalgebra A p).toSubring) : ValuationSubring K :=

/-- **Lemma 5.11.** -/
theorem lemma_5_11
    {k κ : Type u} [Field k] [CharZero k] [Field κ] [Algebra k κ]
    {m : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) (r : Fin (m + 1) → κ) (j : Fin (m + 1))
    (hr0 : r 0 = 0) (hr1 : r (Fin.succ ⟨0, hm⟩) = 0) (hrj : r j = 1)
    (halg : Algebra.IsAlgebraic
      (IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range r) : IntermediateField k κ) κ) :
    ∃ (d' : ℕ) (rows : Fin d' → Fin (m + 1)),
      Function.Injective rows ∧
      (∀ l, rows l ≠ 0 ∧ rows l ≠ Fin.succ ⟨0, hm⟩ ∧ rows l ≠ j) ∧
      LinearIndependent κ (fun l ↦ KaehlerDifferential.D k κ (r (rows l))) ∧
      Submodule.span κ
          (Set.range fun l ↦ KaehlerDifferential.D k κ (r (rows l))) = ⊤ ∧
      d' = Module.finrank κ (Ω[κ⁄k]) := by
  classical
  let axis : Fin (m + 1) := Fin.succ ⟨0, hm⟩
  let good : Set (Fin (m + 1)) := {a | a ≠ 0 ∧ a ≠ axis ∧ a ≠ j}
  let S : Set κ := r '' good
  -- The excluded residues are `0` and `1`, so `L` is generated by `S`.
  have hL : IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range r) = IntermediateField.adjoin k S := by
    apply le_antisymm
    · rw [IntermediateField.adjoin_le_iff]
      rintro _ ⟨a, rfl⟩
      by_cases ha : a ∈ good
      · exact IntermediateField.subset_adjoin k S ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩
      · simp only [good, Set.mem_ofPred_eq, not_and_or, not_not] at ha
        rcases ha with rfl | rfl | rfl
        · rw [hr0]; exact zero_mem _
        · rw [hr1]; exact zero_mem _
        · rw [hrj]; exact one_mem _
    · apply IntermediateField.adjoin.mono
      rintro _ ⟨a, -, rfl⟩
      exact ⟨a, rfl⟩
  -- `L` is generated by the finite set `S`, which therefore contains a transcendence
  -- basis `B` of `L/K` (Definition 5.1, closing sentence; Lang, Thm. VIII.1.1).
  let SL : Set (IntermediateField.adjoin k S) := Subtype.val ⁻¹' S
  have hSL : IntermediateField.adjoin k SL = ⊤ := by
    apply IntermediateField.lift_injective (IntermediateField.adjoin k S)
    rw [IntermediateField.lift_adjoin, IntermediateField.lift_top]
    congr 1
    change Subtype.val '' (Subtype.val ⁻¹' S) = S
    ext z
    refine ⟨fun ⟨w, hw, hwz⟩ => hwz ▸ hw, fun hz => ?_⟩
    exact ⟨⟨z, IntermediateField.subset_adjoin k S hz⟩, hz, rfl⟩
  have hSLfin : SL.Finite :=
    ((Set.toFinite good).image r).preimage Subtype.val_injective.injOn
  obtain ⟨BL, hBLS, hBL⟩ := (definition_5_1_closing (K := k)
    (L := IntermediateField.adjoin k S)).2 SL hSLfin hSL
  -- `κ/L` is algebraic (Lemma 5.10(b)), so `B` is a transcendence basis of `κ/K`.
  have : Algebra.IsAlgebraic (IntermediateField.adjoin k S) κ := hL ▸ halg
  let t : Set κ := Set.range (algebraMap (IntermediateField.adjoin k S) κ ∘ ((↑) : BL → _))
  have ht : IsTranscendenceBasis k ((↑) : t → κ) := hBL.algebraMap_comp.to_subtype_range
  have htS : t ⊆ S := by
    rintro _ ⟨b, rfl⟩
    exact hBLS b.2
  have htfin : t.Finite := (Set.toFinite good |>.image r).subset htS
  let : Fintype t := htfin.fintype
  -- Matsumura, Thm. 26.5: the transcendence basis is a differential basis.
  have hrank : Module.finrank κ (Ω[κ⁄k]) = Fintype.card t :=
    Stafford38.Geometry.kaehlerFinrankOfTranscendenceBasis k κ t (↑) ht
  have hspanT : Submodule.span κ
      (Set.range fun x : t ↦ KaehlerDifferential.D k κ (x : κ)) = ⊤ :=
    Stafford38.Geometry.KaehlerDVRVisibility.kaehler_span_of_isAlgebraic_adjoin
      (fun x : t ↦ (x : κ)) (by simpa using (definition_5_1_g_h ht).1)
  -- Index the basis elements by residues `q_i(0)` with `i ∉ {0, 1, j}`.
  have hpre : ∀ x : t, ∃ a ∈ good, r a = x := fun x ↦ htS x.2
  choose idx hidx hridx using hpre
  let e := Fintype.equivFin t
  let rows : Fin (Fintype.card t) → Fin (m + 1) := fun l ↦ idx (e.symm l)
  have hrows : ∀ l, r (rows l) = (e.symm l : κ) := fun l ↦ hridx _
  have hfam : (fun l ↦ KaehlerDifferential.D k κ (r (rows l))) =
      (fun x : t ↦ KaehlerDifferential.D k κ (x : κ)) ∘ e.symm := by
    funext l
    simp [hrows]
  have hspan : Submodule.span κ
      (Set.range fun l ↦ KaehlerDifferential.D k κ (r (rows l))) = ⊤ := by
    rw [hfam, Set.range_comp, e.symm.surjective.range_eq, Set.image_univ, hspanT]
  have hli : LinearIndependent κ (fun l ↦ KaehlerDifferential.D k κ (r (rows l))) :=
    linearIndependent_of_top_le_span_of_card_eq_finrank hspan.ge
      (by rw [Fintype.card_fin, hrank])
  refine ⟨Fintype.card t, rows, ?_, fun l ↦ hidx _, hli, hspan, hrank.symm⟩
  intro l l' h
  apply e.symm.injective
  apply Subtype.ext
  rw [← hrows, ← hrows, h]

/-- The paper's `ρ : L^{n+1} → L^n`, `ρ(v)_i = (v_i q_0 - q_i v_0) / q_0²`. -/
def rho (q : Fin (n + 1) → L) : (Fin (n + 1) → L) →ₗ[L] (Fin n → L) where
  toFun v i := (v i.succ * q 0 - q i.succ * v 0) / q 0 ^ 2
  map_add' v w := by
    funext i
    simp only [Pi.add_apply]
    ring
  map_smul' c v := by
    funext i
    simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, RingHom.id_apply]
    ring

/-- The kernel of `ρ` is the line `L q`. -/
theorem ker_rho (q : Fin (n + 1) → L) (hq0 : q 0 ≠ 0) :
    LinearMap.ker (rho q) = Submodule.span L {q} := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · intro v hv
    rw [LinearMap.mem_ker] at hv
    rw [Submodule.mem_span_singleton]
    refine ⟨v 0 / q 0, ?_⟩
    funext a
    refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun i ↦ ?_) a
    · simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
      field_simp
    · have hi := congrFun hv i
      simp only [rho_apply, Pi.zero_apply, div_eq_zero_iff, pow_eq_zero_iff, ne_eq,
        OfNat.ofNat_ne_zero, not_false_eq_true, hq0, or_false, sub_eq_zero] at hi
      simp only [Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
      rw [div_mul_eq_mul_div, div_eq_iff hq0]
      linear_combination -hi
  · rw [Submodule.span_le, Set.singleton_subset_iff, SetLike.mem_coe, LinearMap.mem_ker]
    funext i
    simp

/-- The tangent space `Θ_y` at `y = q_i / q_0`. -/
def tangentSpaceAt (q : Fin (n + 1) → L) (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) :
    Submodule L (Fin n → L) :=
  zariskiTangentSpace (dehomogenizedPoint q) (I.map (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap k L)))
Stafford38.Paper.Section5.tangentCone defStafford38/Paper/Section5/TangentCone.lean:57
/-- The affine cone `𝒞 = ρ⁻¹(Θ_y)` over the projective tangent plane. -/
def tangentCone (q : Fin (n + 1) → L) (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) :
    Submodule L (Fin (n + 1) → L) :=
  (tangentSpaceAt q I).comap (rho q)

/-- **Lemma 5.12(a), `dim Θ_y = dim Ω_{F/k}`.**  The tangent space at the
generic point, with coefficients extended to `E ⊇ F`, has the Kähler rank of
the component function field as its dimension. -/
theorem generic_tangent_finrank_eq_component_kaehler_finrank
    {k F E : Type u} [Field k] [Field F] [Field E]
    [Algebra k F] [Algebra k E] [Algebra F E] [IsScalarTower k F E]
    {m : ℕ} {I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)} [I.IsPrime]
    [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k ⧸ I) F]
    [IsScalarTower k (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k ⧸ I) F]
    [IsFractionRing (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k ⧸ I) F]
    (hgen : IntermediateField.adjoin k
      (Set.range (GenericPointKaehlerConormal.genericPoint I F)) = ⊤) :
    Module.finrank E
        (zariskiTangentSpace
          (fun i ↦ algebraMap F E
            (GenericPointKaehlerConormal.genericPoint I F i))
          (I.map (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap k E)))) =
      Module.finrank F (Ω[F⁄k]) :=
  le_antisymm
    (PaperGenericTangentRank.generic_tangent_finrank_le_component_kaehler_finrank
      (E := E) hgen)
    (component_kaehler_finrank_le_generic_tangent_finrank (E := E) hgen)

/-- **`dim Ω_{F/k} = trdeg_k F`.**  For a field `F` generated over `k` by
finitely many elements, in characteristic zero, the Kähler rank is the
transcendence degree (Matsumura, Thm. 26.5), which is finite. -/
theorem component_kaehler_finrank_eq_trdeg
    {k F : Type u} [Field k] [CharZero k] [Field F] [Algebra k F]
    {m : ℕ} (y : Fin m → F)
    (hgen : IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range y) = ⊤) :
    (Module.finrank F (Ω[F⁄k]) : Cardinal) = Algebra.trdeg k F ∧
      Module.finrank F (Ω[F⁄k]) = (Algebra.trdeg k F).toNat := by
  classical
  have : Algebra.IsAlgebraic (Algebra.adjoin k (Set.range y)) F := by
    rw [← IntermediateField.isAlgebraic_adjoin_iff_top, hgen,
      Algebra.isAlgebraic_iff_isIntegral]
    exact Algebra.isIntegral_of_surjective IntermediateField.topEquiv.surjective
  obtain ⟨t, hts, ht⟩ := exists_isTranscendenceBasis_subset (R := k) (Set.range y)
  have htfin : t.Finite := (Set.finite_range y).subset hts
  let : Fintype t := htfin.fintype
  have hrank : Module.finrank F (Ω[F⁄k]) = Fintype.card t :=
    kaehlerFinrankOfTranscendenceBasis k F t (↑) ht
  have hcard : (Fintype.card t : Cardinal) = Algebra.trdeg k F := by
    rw [← Cardinal.mk_fintype]
    exact (definition_5_1_g_h ht).2
  refine ⟨by rw [hrank, hcard], ?_⟩
  rw [← hcard, Cardinal.toNat_natCast, hrank]

/-- **Lemma 5.12(a), `dim_F Ω_{F/K} ≤ d' + 1`.**  For a discrete valuation ring
`V ⊇ K` with fraction field `F`, residue field `κ` and `Ω_{V/K}` finitely
generated: the second fundamental exact sequence for `V → κ` gives
`dim_κ (κ ⊗_V Ω_{V/K}) ≤ d' + 1`, Nakayama's lemma gives that many generators
of `Ω_{V/K}`, and `F ⊗_V Ω_{V/K} = Ω_{F/K}` bounds `dim_F Ω_{F/K}`. -/
theorem lemma_5_12_a_bound
    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra V F] [IsFractionRing V F] [Algebra k F]
    [IsScalarTower k V F] [Module.Finite V (Ω[V⁄k])] :
    Module.finrank F (Ω[F⁄k]) ≤ Module.finrank (ResidueField V) (Ω[ResidueField V⁄k]) + 1 := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := exists_kaehler_generators (k := k) (V := V)
  have h := finrank_fraction_kaehler_le_of_span (F := F) f hf
  rw [Fintype.card_fin] at h
  exact h.trans finrank_residue_tensor_kaehler_le

/-- **Lemma 5.12(a), cone part.** `dim 𝒞 = dim Θ_y + 1`. -/
theorem lemma_5_12_a_cone (q : Fin (n + 1) → L) (hq0 : q 0 ≠ 0)
    (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) :
    Module.finrank L (tangentCone q I) = Module.finrank L (tangentSpaceAt q I) + 1 := by
  classical
  let f : tangentCone q I →ₗ[L] tangentSpaceAt q I :=
    (rho q).restrict (p := tangentCone q I) (q := tangentSpaceAt q I) (fun v hv ↦ hv)
  have hf : Function.Surjective f := by
    rintro ⟨w, hw⟩
    obtain ⟨v, rfl⟩ := rho_surjective q hq0 w
    exact ⟨⟨v, hw⟩, rfl⟩
  have hq : q ∈ tangentCone q I := by
    change rho q q ∈ tangentSpaceAt q I
    have : rho q q = 0 := by
      rw [← LinearMap.mem_ker, ker_rho q hq0]
      exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self q
    rw [this]
    exact zero_mem _
  have hker : Module.finrank L (LinearMap.ker f) = 1 := by
    have hq' : (⟨q, hq⟩ : tangentCone q I) ≠ 0 := by
      intro h
      exact hq0 (congrFun (congrArg Subtype.val h) 0)
    rw [finrank_eq_one_iff_of_nonzero' (⟨⟨q, hq⟩, ?_⟩ : LinearMap.ker f) ?_]
    · rintro ⟨⟨v, hv⟩, hvk⟩
      have hv0 : v ∈ LinearMap.ker (rho q) := by
        rw [LinearMap.mem_ker]
        exact congrArg Subtype.val (LinearMap.mem_ker.mp hvk)
      rw [ker_rho q hq0, Submodule.mem_span_singleton] at hv0
      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := hv0
      exact ⟨c, rfl⟩
    · rw [LinearMap.mem_ker]
      apply Subtype.ext
      change rho q q = 0
      rw [← LinearMap.mem_ker, ker_rho q hq0]
      exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self q
    · intro h
      exact hq' (congrArg Subtype.val h)
  have := LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker f
  rw [LinearMap.range_eq_top.mpr hf, finrank_top, hker] at this
  omega

/-- **Lemma 5.12(b).** If the equations vanish at `y`, then `δq ∈ 𝒞` for every
`K`-derivation `δ` of `L`, and `q ∈ 𝒞`. -/
theorem lemma_5_12_b (q : Fin (n + 1) → L) (hq0 : q 0 ≠ 0)
    (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k))
    (hbase : ∀ f ∈ I,
      MvPolynomial.eval₂ (algebraMap k L) (dehomogenizedPoint q) f = 0) :
    (∀ δ : Derivation k L L, (fun a ↦ δ (q a)) ∈ tangentCone q I) ∧
      q ∈ tangentCone q I := by
  constructor
  · intro δ
    -- `δ(f(y)) = df_y · δy`, so `δy ∈ Θ_y`.
    have htan := Stafford38.Geometry.PowerSeriesArcTangency.derivationVector_mem_zariskiTangentSpace_of_eval₂_eq_zero
      δ I (dehomogenizedPoint q) hbase
    -- Quotient rule: `ρ(δq) = δy`.
    have hquot : rho q (fun a ↦ δ (q a)) = fun i ↦ δ (dehomogenizedPoint q i) := by
      funext i
      rw [rho_apply, dehomogenizedPoint, Derivation.leibniz_div]
      simp only [smul_eq_mul]
      field_simp
    change rho q (fun a ↦ δ (q a)) ∈ tangentSpaceAt q I
    rw [hquot]
    exact htan
  · change rho q q ∈ tangentSpaceAt q I
    have : rho q q = 0 := by
      rw [← LinearMap.mem_ker, ker_rho q hq0]
      exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self q
    rw [this]
    exact zero_mem _

/-- The affine point represented by `q` in the chart `q 0 ≠ 0`. -/
def dehomogenizedPoint (q : Fin (n + 1) → K) : Fin n → K :=
  fun i ↦ q i.succ / q 0

/-- The generic point of the component: images of the coordinates in `F`. -/
def genericPoint (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)) (F : Type*) [Field F]
    [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k ⧸ I) F] : Fin m → F :=
  fun i ↦ algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k ⧸ I) F (Ideal.Quotient.mk I (X i))

/-- **Lemma 5.13.** A row vector annihilating `𝒞` has its affine part
`(ℓ_1, …, ℓ_n)` in `span {df_y : f ∈ 𝔭}`. -/
theorem lemma_5_13 (q : Fin (n + 1) → L) (hq0 : q 0 ≠ 0)
    (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) (ell : Fin (n + 1) → L)
    (hell : ∀ v ∈ tangentCone q I, ∑ a, ell a * v a = 0) :
    coordinateCovector (fun i : Fin n ↦ ell i.succ) ∈
      equationCovectorSpan (dehomogenizedPoint q)
        (I.map (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap k L))) := by
  rw [← affineConormalSpace_eq_equationCovectorSpan, affineConormalSpace,
    Submodule.mem_dualAnnihilator]
  intro w hw
  -- `ρ(𝒞) = Θ_y`.
  have hw' : w ∈ (tangentCone q I).map (rho q) := by
    rw [rho_map_tangentCone q hq0]
    exact hw
  obtain ⟨v, hv, rfl⟩ := hw'
  have hq : q ∈ tangentCone q I := by
    change rho q q ∈ tangentSpaceAt q I
    have : rho q q = 0 := by
      rw [← LinearMap.mem_ker, ker_rho q hq0]
      exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self q
    rw [this]
    exact zero_mem _
  -- `ℓ(q) = 0` and `ℓ(v) = 0` give `Σ ℓ_i ρ(v)_i = 0`.
  have hellq := hell q hq
  have hellv := hell v hv
  rw [Fin.sum_univ_succ] at hellq hellv
  rw [coordinateCovector_apply]
  simp only [rho_apply]
  have hsum : ∑ i : Fin n, ell i.succ * ((v i.succ * q 0 - q i.succ * v 0) / q 0 ^ 2) =
      (q 0 * ∑ i : Fin n, ell i.succ * v i.succ -
        v 0 * ∑ i : Fin n, ell i.succ * q i.succ) / q 0 ^ 2 := by
    rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_div]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ ↦ ?_
    ring
  rw [hsum]
  have h1 : ∑ i : Fin n, ell i.succ * v i.succ = -(ell 0 * v 0) := by linear_combination hellv
  have h2 : ∑ i : Fin n, ell i.succ * q i.succ = -(ell 0 * q 0) := by linear_combination hellq
  rw [h1, h2]
  ring_nf
